name: Albert Park Circuit
grandstandLabels: Start/finish straight and pit/paddock building (Lakeside Dr)
notes: Street-style park circuit around Albert Lake; pits, paddock and main grandstand sit within ~150 m of the start/finish line. 800 m also covers the Lakeside/Aughtie Dr entrance gates.

name: Bahrain International Circuit
grandstandLabels: Pit building, paddock and main grandstand
notes: Desert complex with a large single pit/paddock/grandstand block; car parks and gates extend ~800 m, so 1000 m. 2026 Bahrain round shown as cancelled in ESPN.

name: Baku City Circuit
grandstandLabels: Azadliq Square: pit building, paddock and main grandstands
notes: Street circuit; pits and paddock are temporary structures on Azadliq Square by Government House. Fans also use the Boulevard and Old City sections 1-1.5 km away, which a 900 m photo radius does not cover.

name: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
grandstandLabels: Pit building and Tribuna Principal (main grandstand)
notes: Permanent autodrome; main grandstand and paddock are one block. 1000 m covers the Montmeló gates and car parks. Hosts the 2026 Barcelona Grand Prix.

name: Circuit of the Americas
grandstandLabels: The Tower, pit building and paddock
notes: Existing venues.json record reused (id, coordinates 30.1328,-97.6411, capacity 120000, opened 2012). Tower/paddock and start line 180 m apart; Turn 1 hill and Austin360 Amphitheater add up to ~1 km, so 1200 m.

name: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
grandstandLabels: Pit building and paddock (Casino side of the straight)
notes: Semi-permanent park circuit on Ile Notre-Dame; pits and the start line are 150 m apart and fans move along the whole island. 900 m.

name: Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez
grandstandLabels: Pit building and paddock beside the main straight
Start of the main straight / Turn 17 Peraltada approach
notes: City park circuit through Magdalena Mixhuca; the Foro Sol stadium is built into the infield (Turns 12-14). Pit complex and start node are ~440 m apart, so two points at 1200 m.

name: Hungaroring
grandstandLabels: Pit building, paddock and main grandstand
End of start/finish straight and Turn 1 grandstands
notes: Natural-amphitheatre circuit; main stand and Turn 1 are 250 m apart. 1000 m.

name: Autodromo Jose Carlos Pace
aliases: Autodromo de Interlagos Jose Carlos Pace
grandstandLabels: Pit building, paddock and start/finish (Reta Oposta side)
notes: Compact hill circuit in the Interlagos district; Wikidata point (400 m away) is at the Descida do Lago end and is not used. 900 m covers the Setor A/B grandstands.

name: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
grandstandLabels: Pit building and paddock with start/finish, south end of the Corniche
notes: Fast street circuit along the Red Sea corniche; pits at the south end. 2026 round (Saudi Arabian GP) is listed as cancelled by ESPN. Temporary grandstands along the 6.2 km, so 1200 m around the pit complex only.

name: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
grandstandLabels: Pit building and paddock at Harmon Ave and Koval Ln (start/finish)
Las Vegas Boulevard Strip grandstands near Flamingo Rd
notes: Night street race on the Strip; the pit building is 1.2 km east of the Strip section. Two points at 1500 m. Wikidata has no coordinate for the circuit (point is on the Grand Prix event item).

name: Lusail International Circuit
notes: Desert circuit with a very long pit building; start line and Wikidata paddock point are 470 m apart. 1200 m. ESPN spells it Losail.

name: Madring
grandstandLabels: IFEMA Madrid exhibition centre (paddock and hospitality)
notes: New semi-street circuit around the IFEMA Madrid fairground, host of the 2026 Spanish Grand Prix (first race Sep 2026). Start and IFEMA centre are 220 m apart. 1200 m.

name: Marina Bay Street Circuit
grandstandLabels: Pit Building and paddock (Republic Blvd) with start/finish
notes: Night street race; Zone grandstands, Padang and Esplanade sections stretch 1.5 km west of the Pit Building, so 1100 m around the pit point is a compromise.

name: Miami International Autodrome
grandstandLabels: Hard Rock Stadium plaza and Turn 1 grandstands
notes: Temporary circuit built around Hard Rock Stadium (which is its own venue in the catalog) and its car parks; the stadium point is 190 m from the track. Pit/start node and the stadium are ~190 m apart; 1500 m because the Turn 1 and Turns 11-16 grandstands are 700 m from the pits.

name: Circuit de Monaco
grandstandLabels: Pit straight, Boulevard Albert 1er (pit lane and paddock)
notes: Whole circuit is inside ~1.5 km in a tiny principality; harbour paddock, Sainte Devote and Casino grandstands are 400-500 m apart. Two points with 1200 m. Wikidata/Ergast point sits at the harbour west end (60 m off track) and is not used.

name: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
grandstandLabels: Start/finish straight: pit building, podium and Tribuna Centrale
notes: Royal Park circuit; pit/paddock complex and Parabolica exit are 375 m apart, the Prima Variante stands another 600 m north. 1200 m. Wikidata point (45.6206, 9.2894) is at Curva Grande, 700 m from the pits, so it is not used.

name: Red Bull Ring
grandstandLabels: Pit building, start/finish and main grandstand
notes: Compact permanent circuit in a valley; grandstands, paddock and Red Bull Mobile Home area are within ~500 m. 1000 m covers the camp sites on the hillsides.

name: Sepang International Circuit
grandstandLabels: Main grandstand, pit building and paddock
Pit straight west end / Turn 1 grandstands
notes: Hosted F1 1999-2017 and the 2026 round (Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia). Twin-grandstand pit complex; pit building and the pit straight west end are 260 m apart. Not near Kuala Lumpur city center (about 55 km).

name: Shanghai International Circuit
notes: Largest grandstand complex on the calendar (200,000 capacity); start line node and Wikidata building point are 260 m apart, so two points and 1100 m.

name: Silverstone Circuit
grandstandLabels: Hamilton Straight: The Wing, pit lane and Wing paddock
notes: Biggest site on the calendar (175,000 capacity) with grandstands spread over ~3 km, huge campsites and the Wing; 1500 m (the maximum) around two points.

name: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
grandstandLabels: La Source: pit building, paddock and start/finish
notes: 7 km track in the Ardennes forest; the pit complex and Eau Rouge are 900 m apart and fans camp around both. Two points at 1500 m. ESPN lists the town as Stavelot. The Ergast/Wikidata point (50.4372, 5.9714) is 240 m off the track and is not used.

name: Suzuka Circuit
grandstandLabels: Start/finish, pit building and main grandstand
notes: Figure-eight circuit inside the Suzuka Circuit Park with a Ferris wheel, hotel and 155,000 capacity; main grandstand and park gates within ~700 m. 1000 m.

name: Yas Marina Circuit
grandstandLabels: Pit building and paddock with start/finish
notes: Yas Island complex with the W Hotel straddling the track and the marina 390 m from the pits. 1100 m.

name: Circuit Zandvoort
grandstandLabels: Pit building, paddock and main grandstand
notes: Seaside-dunes circuit where the pit complex and the far-end grandstands are 170 m apart; campsites and the beach are within ~1 km. 1000 m. F1 returned in 2021 after 1985.

name: Hockenheimring
grandstandLabels: Motodrom: start/finish, pit building and main grandstand
notes: Hosted F1 2018 and 2019. Stadium-like Motodrom keeps the grandstands inside ~400 m; 900 m for the car parks and gates.

name: Autodromo Enzo e Dino Ferrari
aliases: Autodromo Internazionale Enzo e Dino Ferrari
notes: Hosted F1 2020-2022 and 2024-2025. Park circuit on the Santerno river; pits and Tamburello are 420 m apart. ESPN calls the 2020-2025 events Emilia Romagna GP.

name: Istanbul Park
grandstandLabels: Pit building, paddock and main grandstand
notes: Hosted F1 2005-2011, 2020 and 2021 (Tuzla, Asian side, ~45 km from the centre). Single pit/grandstand block, 900 m.

name: Autodromo Internazionale del Mugello
notes: Hosted a single F1 round, the 2020 Tuscan Grand Prix (Ferrari's 1000th GP), behind closed doors apart from a small crowd. 1000 m covers the hill grandstands.

name: Nurburgring Grand Prix Circuit
notes: F1 used the 5.148 km GP circuit in 2020 (Eifel GP); the Nordschleife next door is a separate track. Pits/paddock and Mercedes-Arena are one cluster, 900 m.

name: Circuit Paul Ricard
notes: Hosted F1 2018-2019, 2021-2022. Permanent autodrome with a long pit building; two points 160 m apart, 1000 m.

name: Autodromo Internacional do Algarve
grandstandLabels: Pit building and main grandstand on the pit straight
notes: Hosted F1 2020 and 2021. Hilly rollercoaster circuit with the pit straight on a slope; 900 m.

name: Sochi Autodrom
grandstandLabels: Pit building and paddock beside Fisht Stadium
notes: Hosted F1 2018-2021 (Russian GP dropped from 2022). Circuit weaves through the Olympic Park; pit building and main straight are 300 m apart, 1000 m.

name: Scandinavian Raceway
notes: F1 host 1973-1978 (Swedish GP; Brabham fan-car win 1978). Coordinate from Wikipedia text; Wikidata item not resolved, lower confidence; OSM Nominatim agrees within 170 m.

name: Brands Hatch
notes: F1 host 1964-1986 (British / European GP, alternating with Silverstone). No clean official F1 lap record in the source, so lapRecord is null.

name: Buddh International Circuit
notes: F1 host 2011-2013 (Indian GP).

name: Autodromo Oscar y Juan Galvez
notes: F1 host 1953-1981 and 1995-1998 (Argentine GP). Centerline node used for the pits; lap record and turns not sourced, so left null.

name: Dijon-Prenois
notes: F1 host 1974, 1977, 1979, 1981, 1982 and 1984 (French/Swiss GP). No clean official F1 lap record on the current 3.801 km layout, so lapRecord is null.

name: Autodromo do Estoril
notes: F1 host 1984-1996 (Portuguese GP). No Wikidata/Ergast point checked beyond the site coordinate; centerline node used for the pits.

name: Fuji Speedway
notes: F1 host 1976-1977 and 2007-2008 (Japanese GP); current track is the 2005 Tilke layout.

name: Indianapolis Motor Speedway
notes: F1 US GP used the infield road course 2000-2007 (Indy 500 counted in the World Championship 1950-1960). Largest grandstand capacity on Earth; 2.5 mile oval, so 1500 m around the Pagoda only.

name: Circuito del Jarama
notes: F1 host 1968-1981 (Spanish GP). Lap record is for the 1980 layout.

name: Circuito de Jerez - Angel Nieto
notes: F1 host 1986-1990 (Spanish GP) and 1994, 1997 (European GP; 1997 title decider).

name: Kyalami Grand Prix Circuit
notes: F1 host 1967-1985 and 1992-1993. Lap record is for the 4.261 km 1992 F1 layout; the current GP circuit is 4.529 km.

name: Circuit de Nevers Magny-Cours
notes: F1 host 1991-2008 (French GP). Permanent circuit still used for motorcycle and club racing.

name: Watkins Glen International
notes: F1 US GP host 1961-1980. Centerline node used for the pits; lap record and turns not sourced, so left null.

name: Korea International Circuit
notes: F1 host 2010-2013 (Korean GP). Coordinate from the Wikipedia article (Wikidata has no P625 on the circuit item), rounded to 4 decimals, so lower confidence; OSM Nominatim agrees within 290 m.

name: Circuit Zolder
notes: F1 host 1973-1984 (Belgian GP, alternating with Nivelles/Spa). Lap record is for the 1984 F1 layout.
